title: A Bullied Coward Stopped The Deadliest Fighter Alive With One Punch . . . (Full Story)

segments.say: A school coward who once begged for his life just *punched* the deadliest man alive, and the whole room froze.
That man is Goomoonryong, the Nine Arts Dragon, and seconds earlier he *butchered* a whole building full of fighters.
The kid in front of him can barely stand, covered in blood, but he still *refuses* to run away.
To see how it got here, go back to a very ordinary *school*, where nothing special happens to anybody.
Shi-woon Lee is a quiet high school kid, and Changho's gang uses him as a *punching* bag every single day.
Every hallway is a trap, and he comes home with a new *bruise* more often than homework.
Today the gang wants sixty thousand won from him, and he has no clue how he will *pay* it.
Then Sae-hee, the girl he secretly likes, walks down the hallway and sees his battered *face*.
She asks what happened, and he is so ashamed that he can barely look at her.
He snaps at her to stay out of it, and he hates himself the second the words *leave* his mouth.
Meanwhile a new substitute teacher walks in wearing a flowery *shirt*, and asks a student where the school office is.
His name is Han Chun-woo, and he looks like a washed-up beach *bum* who got lost on vacation.
He spots the bruises and calls Shi-woon a *coward* who cannot hit back, which is a hell of an intro.
Rude, but not exactly *wrong*.
Han took a quiet job at a quiet school to hide from his past, and he picked the worst *one*.
In class, Shi-woon keeps his head down and prays that nobody, especially the new teacher, will notice *him*.
Then Changho barks at the teacher to stop screwing around and start the lesson, like he *owns* the place.
Han just grins, tells the whole class to open their books, and somehow Changho *shuts* up.
Nobody has ever made Changho *back* down before, and Shi-woon starts to wonder about this guy.
That night, outside a Muay Thai gym, a pack of drunk thugs *surrounds* the strange new teacher.
The thugs demand that Han pay up for a drink he never *ordered*, and he just smiles at them.
He thanks them for the lovely evening, and then the first chair goes *flying*.
Han takes one thug's insult as a *compliment*, then kicks the whole room across the floor like a video game.
Shi-woon has no idea yet, but the clown in the flowery shirt is no ordinary *teacher*.
Meanwhile the vice principal is *fuming*, because a man in a flowery shirt is not his idea of a professional.
Even the new female teacher tries to flirt with him, and he dodges her like she is a *tax* collector.
Han wants his past kept a *secret*, but Shi-woon has already seen too much.
At lunch Changho calls for Shi-woon, and the whole classroom goes *quiet*.
Changho's boys are not done with Shi-woon, and the next morning they drag him into the *bathroom*.
One bully blows smoke in his face and tells him to shut up and *take* it.
They throw him around until he is on the floor, and all he can do is *apologize*.
Then they leave him there laughing, and remind him not to forget the money next *week*.
He drags himself back into the hallway, and every student *watches*, including the girl he likes.
Sae-hee runs up and asks if he is okay, and he rips his arm *away* from her.
He yells that it does not concern her, and she just stands there *stunned*.
He knows she is the one person who actually *cares*, and that makes it hurt more.
That is the moment Shi-woon decides the world would be better off without *him*.
Up on the school roof, he starts to think the only way out of this life is *down*.
He climbs up to the ledge, and the second he slips, he screams *save* me.
And who hears him? The weird substitute, who tells him to hurry up and *jump*.
For a second, Han's face goes serious, because this is no *prank*.
Han yanks him up, and makes him promise he will never jump from this roof *again*.
Then the rusty railing *snaps*, because of course it does.
They both fall off the roof and crash straight onto the vice principal's brand new *car*.
Shi-woon gets up with barely a scratch, and has no idea how he is *alive*.
Even Han looks confused, and wonders why he bothered to save this *kid*.
The vice principal's car is totaled, and he grills the whole school about who did *it*.
Students whisper about the fall, and the vice principal sniffs through the wreck like a *detective*.
Han just smiles and swears he saw absolutely *nothing*, which is a lie, and a beautiful one.
Then the vice principal locks the roof for good, and swears he will find whoever did *this*.
Han takes a phone call that night, and the voice on the other end he calls *master*.
Master has one rule for him, which is that nobody at this school can ever learn who he *is*.
Next morning, Shi-woon gets called to the teachers' office, and the whole fight gets dragged *out*.
His teacher slaps him across the face and demands to know who beat him *up*.
Then Changho walks in, smiles, and says it was just a little *misunderstanding*.
The teacher forces both sides to shake hands, and declares the whole thing *settled*.
Changho shakes his hand with a smile, and whispers that he will be *seeing* him again.
That smile is not a truce, that smile is a *warning*.
At home his mom drops off some groceries for five minutes, then leaves for work *again*.
He asks if he can change schools, and she asks if something happened *there*.
He says no, because what kind of son adds more trouble to a mom who is already *tired*?
So he swallows it all, and does what he does best, which is *nothing*.
At night he lies awake with his phone, hoping that someone, anyone, will *call*.
At school he hides on a bench during break, hoping the gang will not *find* him.
They find him anyway, and Changho asks where his *girlfriend* is.
Then he orders Shi-woon to bring Sae-hee behind the gym after class, or else you know what *happens*.
Terrified, Shi-woon runs to the one adult who has any strength, the flowery shirt *teacher*.
He begs for help, because he has nobody *else*.
Han says he is only a temporary teacher, gone in two months, so it is not his *problem*.
He tells Shi-woon to solve his own problems, then walks off with his hands in his *pockets*.
Shi-woon screams that he is a coward, and that is exactly *why* he is asking for help.
He asks him straight out if he is a martial arts master, and Han panics and *denies* everything.
Han keeps walking, and Shi-woon is left alone in the *hallway*.
The next day, Sae-hee tells him that if there is anything she can do, she wants to *help*.
He looks down, and he cannot make himself tell her the *truth*.
Meanwhile the vice principal threatens to fire Han by the end of the day, and Han just keeps *smiling*.
So that afternoon he does the bravest and dumbest thing he has ever *done*.
The gang waits behind the gym, and asks where Sae-hee *is*.
He walks behind the gym alone, and tells the gang that Sae-hee is *not* coming.
Changho's boys show him exactly how much that sentence will *cost*.
He swings back, screaming that he is going to *change*, and it is the first punch he has ever thrown.
His eyes finally change, and he stops looking like a *victim*.
Then he loses badly, and lies there bleeding, but he does not *regret* it.
He lies on the ground laughing through the blood, because for once he hit *back*.
Bloody and limping, he crawls back to Han and drops to his *knees*.
He tells him he fought back, and that is why he wants to learn how to *fight*.
That took more guts than any punch.
Han finally says yes, but only if Shi-woon is willing to risk his *life*.
Han asks if he still wants to learn after hearing that, and Shi-woon says *yes*.
Then he drives the boy to a bridge at night, and tells him to *jump*.
Shi-woon stares down at the water, shaking, and for a second he thinks it is *over*.
He asks one last question, will Han really teach him if he jumps, and Han *panics* a little inside.
Then he jumps, and for one long second he is *sure* he is dead.
Underwater, the world goes quiet, and he wonders whether his life was ever worth *anything*.
Han hauls him out, ruins his fancy shoes, and drags him to the *hospital*, complaining the whole way.
Imagine nearly dying just to sign up for karate *class*.
In the hospital bed, Shi-woon smiles, because the man in the flowery shirt is now his *teacher*.
Han makes him promise never to jump again, which is honestly *fair*.
Shi-woon asks if he will really teach him, and Han stays silent, which is as close to *yes* as he gets.
Across the city, a group of old men who run the hidden world of the *Murim* whisper in the dark.
They talk about a legendary killing technique, and a man who may still be *alive*.
They call that man Goomoonryong, the Nine Arts *Dragon*, and he is their worst disaster.
Meanwhile the guy they are hunting is smoking on the school roof, without a *care* in the world.
Then a man in a black suit and sunglasses walks up *behind* him.
Han just smirks, and asks if he *disturbed* him that much.
The fight starts, and it ends about as fast as it *started*.
Then the health teacher, Shiho, corners Han in her office, and he looks like a man about to be *devoured*.
She knows exactly who he *is*, and she is not impressed by the disguise.
She keeps flirting anyway, and Han keeps dodging, like she is a debt *collector*.
A Murim legend just beat a man in a suit, and he still screams when a woman grabs his *shirt*.
Meanwhile Changho's gang catches Shi-woon again, and this time nobody *stops* them.
He ends up face down on the ground, barely *breathing*.
Han shows up, throws him over his shoulder, and complains that he is getting *tired* of carrying this kid.
Shi-woon whispers it again, please teach me how to *fight*.
He wakes up wiping his face, and then he freaks out when he realizes whose room he is *in*.
He wakes up in a strange bed, and the health teacher is already making him *breakfast*.
She asks why a boy like him wants to learn martial arts, and he has no good *answer*.
He thanks her, because somehow his body feels better than it has in *years*.
Han leads him to the school field, tosses him a ball, and says to throw it with all his *might*.
So the real training begins, and the first test is a pure *disaster*.
Sit-ups, push-ups, long jump, a hundred meter dash, and Shi-woon fails them *all*.
Han looks at his body and tells him to come back when he can at least handle a *car*.
Laps around the track, then more laps, and if he faints, Han says *more* laps.
Shi-woon throws up, collapses and cries, but he is back on that field the next *morning*.
Shiho sees how hard he trains and finds it hard to *watch*.
Meanwhile in class, Han teaches English by reading Tom Sawyer, which is not exactly the lesson *plan*.
Sae-hee notices that he is limping, and tells him she was *worried*.
He promises himself that he will not run *away*, no matter how hard this gets.
Two weeks in, he can run one lap without throwing up, which for him is basically a *miracle*.
Shiho tells him his body is the real problem, because his blood cannot keep up with the *training*.
Then she hands him a strange pill, and warns that in the worst case, he could *die*.
He swallows it anyway, because he has nothing left to *lose*.
At night, Shiho watches him run laps, because she cannot stand by and watch it *happen*.
Far from school, a young Alliance fighter swears the Dragon is his master's enemy, and the vengeance is *his*.
A black limousine glides through the night, full of men who want Han *dead*.
Then a gang boss named Song starts hunting the Nine Arts *Dragon*, and he brings a lot of friends.
His men are told to find him, and to hold him there until the boss *arrives*.
So one night in the park, Han is lighting a cigarette when a crowd of thugs *surrounds* him.
They crack their knuckles, and they honestly think the night is going to be *easy*.
Han just smokes, says he does not want any *trouble*, and offers them a chance to leave.
Nobody takes the offer, because nobody ever does.
Then Song steps out of the dark, and Han finally bares his dragon *tattoo*.
That mark belongs to the Nine Arts Dragon, a legend of the Murim, where martial arts clans *rule*.
Song's men laugh, and that is the last *mistake* they ever make.
Song shows off his famous iron hand, and Han tells him it is quite *impressive*.
He says that to win in one blow, he needs a soul-crushing *strike*.
One punch later, the boss's iron hand turns into a bloody *mess*.
In a car across the street, two men in suits quietly watch the whole *thing*.
Han flicks his cigarette away, and walks off like nothing *happened*.
Never insult a man holding a cigarette.
Word gets around, and Shi-woon finally understands why his teacher was never afraid of *Changho*.
Han hates attention, but trouble finds him anyway, like a bad *sequel* nobody asked for.
Back at school, Changho's gang corners Shi-woon again, expecting the usual *routine*, like he is a vending machine for punches.
This time he does not crawl, and the whole hallway hears the *crack* of a fist.
Main-character energy, finally unlocked.
Han hears about the punch, and warns him that power is a drug, and drunk fighters ruin *themselves*.
Then a Lamborghini rolls into the faculty parking lot, and the vice principal cannot stop *staring* at it.
Whoever owns it, the vice principal looks ready to cry about his own *car*.
The vice principal is so furious that he starts screaming at a janitor who has nothing to do with *it*.
Shi-woon falls asleep in the infirmary, soaked in sweat, and Sae-hee is the one who finds *him*.
She says she missed him at school, and he realizes how much he missed *her*.
Changho's gang decides he needs a little re-education, and they gang up on him *again*.
He stands there taking it, and he does not say a single *word*.
Then he limps down the hallway, whispering that he will find out what he can *do*.
Then men in expensive suits roll up in a black *Maybach*, and every student stops to stare.
Their young master is hunting the Nine Arts Dragon, and he is *not* polite about it.
In this world, martial arts clans hide behind ordinary jobs, and their fights decide who runs the *shadows*.
Behind closed doors, the Nine Clans argue over who will find the Dragon *first*.
The young master is also hunting Shiho, and he swears she cannot hide *forever*.
Two thugs show up at the school asking for the female teacher *Shiho*.
They hold a knife to Shi-woon, and he has no idea what they are *talking* about.
He bleeds and shakes, but he still does not give them what they *want*.
Han teaches him to breathe slowly and deeply, because he says a strong body is only the *start*.
He calls it ki, the energy inside every martial artist, and says it matters more than any *muscle*.
Han says ki normally takes years to learn, and Shi-woon has about two *months*.
Goku had a scouter, but Shi-woon only has a *stomachache*.
Meanwhile the Nine Clans meet around a tea table, and evil men love their *tea*.
One elder is certain the Dragon is still hiding in this *city*, and he wants him found.
Shiho takes him for a ride in her Lamborghini, and he steps out dizzy, like he left a *roller* coaster.
He is still weak, but for the first time in his life, he *shows* up every single day.
Then one night he finds a frightened white-haired girl on a dark road, and tells her it is *okay*.
Her name is Sosul, and the next thing he knows, he is carrying her down a dark *highway*.
She is being hunted, and a pack of bikers is *chasing* them both.
He is just a kid with a few weeks of training, and he runs until his lungs *burn*.
He tells her he is sorry, because he cannot run any *further*.
Then the lights of the bikes close in, and he is sure this is the *end*.
That is when Han appears and screams, do you know whose *disciple* you are messing with?
The bikers hear the name Goomoonryong, and the color drains from their *faces*.
Han turns their whole gang into scrap metal, and it is a full Hulk *smash*.
That is what a teacher is for.
Sosul is the daughter of a powerful clan, and her father presses a Phoenix seal into her *hands*.
Shi-woon wakes up with the girl safe beside him, and he has no idea what he has *signed* up for.
Hunted by powerful enemies, she ends up hiding in his apartment, and he promises to *protect* her.
Shi-woon, who has never talked to a girl, now has one living at his *place*.
He makes her breakfast, pats her on the head, and tells her not to *worry*.
Sosul asks if he wants to be a Murim person, and he says he only wants to protect his *friends*.
Another Alliance man arrives in the city with a cold smile, and says he wants to meet Goomoonryong *soon*.
Han teaches him to throw a punch step by step, and Shi-woon answers *yes* sir like a soldier.
Then he hits a tree so hard that it shakes, and for once the tree loses.
Then Sae-hee is snatched off the street by a van, and Shi-woon screams her name as he *chases* it.
He tracks the thugs to a warehouse and walks in alone with his fists *up*, shaking but standing.
The training kicks in, and for once he is the one *swinging*.
He saves her, and Sae-hee asks softly if he was really *scared*, and he admits he was.
Main-character energy, round two.
Then a calm man in a black suit stops them on a night road and asks about *Goomoonryong*.
Shi-woon says he has never heard that name, and the man *smiles*, because he never said it was a person.
So he tells Sae-hee to run, and he stands his ground *alone*.
He shoves her into a taxi, slams the door, and turns to face whatever is *coming*.
The man in black just stands in the road, calm as a dentist, and Shi-woon's legs begin to *shake*.
The man does not even try hard, and Shi-woon is bleeding in *seconds*.
Every punch he throws gets blocked, and every punch the man throws puts him on the *ground*.
But he tells the man he does not care who he is, or what clan he *serves*.
He says that if the man wants to get past him, he will have to defeat him *first*.
He cannot win, and everyone watching knows it, but he refuses to *quit*.
In the end the man in black walks away, and promises they will meet *again*.
Shi-woon wakes up bandaged, and Sosul stays by his bed all night, *worried* sick.
Meanwhile an Alliance fighter says he has only one goal, to take the lives of those who killed his *master*.
Rumors travel fast, and soon every gangster in the city is whispering about the Nine Arts *Dragon*.
Shi-woon only wants to learn, and tells Han he will protect his friends *one* day.
Han shrugs, but he keeps teaching him, and Shi-woon *grins* like an idiot.
After the fight with the man in black, Shi-woon ends up in a cast, and Shiho drives everyone to the beach to cheer him *up*.
Sosul blushes, and makes him promise to take her to an amusement park *next*.
That night Han drags him to a rooftop, and he is not in a good *mood*.
He yells that Shi-woon is an idiot, because the Murim will find them *all*.
Then he gives him one last lesson, a footwork technique, and tells him to watch *carefully*.
If Shi-woon turns back into a coward while he is gone, Han will not take him back as a *disciple*.
Then he drives off in his Lamborghini, and Shi-woon waves like a little *kid*.
An Alliance man with glasses reports that he has found the Nine Arts Dragon's *hideout*.
It is a high school, which is the last place anyone would *look*.
Back at school, Sae-hee catches up with him, worried that he has been *distant*.
Changho swears he will show everyone what happens to people who mess with *him*.
Sae-hee apologizes for being too scared to help him, and cries *softly*.
Shi-woon tells her that from now on, he will not back down while he has someone to *protect*.
Shi-woon sits in class for the first time in ages, and thinks about how much he has *changed*.
Changho does not take that well, and one afternoon he shows up with a baseball *bat*.
He swings it down the hallway, screaming that he will kill them both, and nobody can *stop* him.
The old chief of the Alliance walks into the school in his kimono, like he *owns* it.
That same afternoon, a black car pulls up outside, and men in suits walk in looking for *Shi-woon*.
The Alliance has figured out that he is Goomoonryong's disciple, and they want to use him as *bait*.
Shi-woon hears them coming, and decides that he will not be a burden to his teacher *anymore*.
He calls Han, but all he gets is a busy *tone*.
So he runs, and a van full of strangers in sunglasses pulls up beside *him*.
They say they are not kidnappers, they are here to *help*.
A black van chases them through the city, and the driver handles it like an action *movie*.
One of them says that Han is the most infamous villain in the *Murim*.
Shi-woon yells that he will not sit around with people who speak badly of *Sunsengnim*.
In their tower, the old masters decide to use the boy to *trap* the Dragon.
The Alliance watches the city through cameras, and one man complains that there is no clear shot of his *face*.
They are sure that Goomoonryong will walk right into it, because he cares about his *disciple*.
Ten old men against one teacher.
Years ago, Han lost control of his rage, and the Murim elders branded him a *monster*.
The Alliance decides the best way to catch him is to build a trap around the *tower*.
Han gets a call saying his disciple is at the tower, and he hears the trap in the caller's *voice*.
The old chief is furious, because nobody insults the Alliance and walks *away*.
So the chief orders his men to go after the kid, and they *hunt* him.
Meanwhile Shi-woon passes out in the back seat of the van, and the men in sunglasses call him totally *wasted*.
Shi-woon charges his dead phone in a stranger's van, and decides he has to reach the tower *himself*.
Then he realizes the elders are tracking his phone, which is a rookie *mistake*.
So he tells the driver to stop the car, because he will lure the trackers *away* himself.
He steps out into the street alone, and says it ends *here*.
That is not a plan, that is a *dare*.
Han storms into the city in a white sports car, with Shiho at his *side*.
Shiho tells him she will follow him even to the depths of *hell*.
A huge crowd gathers around the business tower, and nobody knows why they are *there*.
The crowd waits like a fan club, because a Goomoonryong sighting beats any rock *concert*.
Martial artists beg the guards to let them in, like it is a sold-out *show*.
The Alliance has a welcome committee, and a man in a striped suit introduces himself with a *smile*.
He promises to show everyone his skills, and he smiles a little too *wide*.
Han looks up at the tower and mutters about those old farts, not in the mood to *wait*.
Meanwhile Shi-woon makes it to the tower door, and the door is *locked*.
He begs the guards to let him in, and they tell him it is *useless*.
He raises his fist and says that if they refuse him, he will use *force*.
He tells them that losing a fight is still better than not fighting at *all*.
Then he swings, loses, and sits on the floor gasping for *air*.
Inside, Han and Shiho cut through the Alliance, and the stairs fill up with fallen *fighters*.
Then Shiho opens her jacket, whose lining can fill the stairwell with poison gas, and offers to take everyone to hell *together*.
Poison gas fills the stairwell, the Alliance men panic, and somewhere in the chaos, Shi-woon slips *inside*.
Han screams at him for coming, but Shiho admits that without Shi-woon, they would both be *dead*.
Han tells her it is not her fight, and she says she is going with him to the *end*.
Meanwhile the chief screams at his own men, because the Sunwoo family's lady, Sosul, slipped *away* from them.
Then the fire alarm goes off, and every coward in the building runs for the *stairs*.
Han climbs up anyway, alone, with a smile on his *face*, like a boss walking into the final level.
Nobody can tell if he is brave or insane, and honestly, same.
On the roof, the old chief welcomes him, and tells Goomoonryong he is a little *late*.
Shiho and Shi-woon stumble out of the smoke behind him, and realize it was a trap from the *start*.
Han taunts the old men to come at him all at once, and the chief takes him on *himself*.
The chief says his recklessness is his biggest weakness, just like his master, who was more wild beast than martial *artist*.
Han is still drained from the poison on the stairs, and in front of the whole Alliance, the legend actually *loses*.
The chief says he does not want to kill a young man with a promising *future*.
Han tells him not to make him laugh, but he is running on *fumes*.
He drops to his knees, bleeding, and tells his dead master that he is *sorry*.
Shiho walks over, kneels beside him, and asks if he is *alright*.
Then Shiho pours in the ki she drew out of Shi-woon, and Han's empty ki starts to flow *again*.
The chief sees the Dragon getting back up, and he pulls out a *gun*.
The gun goes off, and Shiho is the one who goes *down*.
Han catches her, and screams for her to open her *eyes*.
He holds her on the roof, bleeding, and cannot do a single thing to *save* her.
And then something inside Han *breaks*, and the whole roof goes quiet.
The old rage takes over, and something terrifying takes Han's *place*.
He tears through the Alliance's best, and every blow shakes the *tower*, like Saitama on a bad day.
Bodies fly, glass shatters, and the old men finally look *scared*.
That is not a human anymore.
Kang-sung looks at the monster Han has become, and asks what *state* he is in.
Then he charges in, the one man in the Alliance who might actually stand a *chance*.
Down in the rain, Sosul steps up and commands her people to protect *Shi-woon*.
Then a bleeding Shi-woon staggers toward him and asks, Sunsengnim, can you *hear* me?
Han does not know him anymore, and he nearly punches his own student to *death*.
But Shi-woon keeps getting back up, and says, this is not the Sunsengnim I *believe* in.
He says he was a coward who thought of ending his life, and Han *saved* him.
He says that if it were not for Sunsengnim, he would not even be *here*.
And then he throws one *punch*.
That punch stops the Nine Arts Dragon *cold*, and every fighter on the roof asks if that kid really did it.
Then Han strikes his own student straight *through*, and the whole roof thinks he just killed him.
Han goes after the chief, but Kang-sung, the Alliance's top fighter, says the old man is as good as *dead*.
He tells Han that he should hurry up and get his disciple *treated*.
Han just laughs and says that kid was only a *toy*, never his disciple, while Shi-woon lies there bleeding.
Han asks if he knows who killed his master, and Kang-sung says he does, but does not *blame* him.
That should have ended it, but two monsters like that never talk things out, so the ground starts *shaking*.
The Alliance has seen enough, and its men yell at Kang-sung to get on the *chopper*.
He promises there will always be another *chance*, and he climbs on board.
Their helicopter lifts off with the old chief, and the roof finally goes *silent*.
Shi-woon wakes up in a hospital bed, and the first thing he feels is that something inside him is *missing*.
Kang-sung tells him his people brought him to the hospital, and that he told his mom it was a car *accident*.
Then a doctor explains that Han destroyed his ki center, so he can never use martial arts *again*.
Shi-woon asks if Sunsengnim really tried to *kill* him.
Han probably did it to *save* him, because a boy with no martial arts is no disciple to hunt.
Shi-woon begs the empty room for an answer, and nobody *answers*.
Han, Shiho and even Sosul vanish like they never existed, and Shi-woon keeps calling, but nobody *answers*.
Back at school, Sae-hee finds him and says his mom has been worried *sick*.
Changho has been suspended indefinitely, which is the one good piece of news in all *this*.
All Han leaves behind is a video on a new phone, teaching him one more ki *technique*.
Meanwhile Han is out there wrecking drug lords around the world, and the Murim's pride is in *pieces*.
The Sunwoo clan elders still want Shi-woon as their heir, because a boy who cannot fight makes an obedient *puppet*.
Men in suits show up at his school and bow to him, and Shi-woon says they have the wrong *person*.
They do not budge, they came for Goomoonryong's disciple, the clan's new *heir*.
The punching bag who begged for his life stopped the Nine Arts Dragon with one punch, and that is the *end*.
